title: M-A080326-01 Update Regarding Batch Zero Timelines and Processes
key_claim: ERCOT suspended the Batch Zero large-load classification notifications due on 7 August 2026 after the Governor's directive, and will seek a good cause exception from the PUCT ahead of its 20 August 2026 open meeting.
frame_summary: ERCOT is arguing that it cannot advance any data-centre large load through interconnection until a verification process demanded by the state has been completed, so the study timetable is suspended rather than adjusted.
verbatim_quote: ERCOT will not notify each Interconnecting Distribution Service Provider and Transmission Service Provider of how any Large Load is classified in the Batch Zero Interconnection Study by August 7, 2026.
verbatim_list: ERCOT will file, in advance of the Public Utility Commission of Texas's (PUCT's) August 20, 2026 open meeting, a request for a good cause exception related to the timelines and process for Batch Zero set forth in ERCOT Planning Guide Sections 5 and 9.
notes: Primary Tier 1 record of the suspension. The Governor's letter PDF and the gov.texas.gov news post both returned empty bodies to the fetcher, so the directive is cited through ERCOT and the Texas Tribune instead.

title: FERC Launches Aggressive Targeted Action to Speed Large Load Integration
date_evidence:
News Releases

# FERC Launches Aggressive Targeted Action to Speed Large Load Integration

---

June 18, 2026
key_claim: FERC issued section 206 show-cause orders to all six RTOs and ISOs, requiring them within 60 days either to justify their existing large-load tariffs or to file changes, and within 30 days to report how they will ensure adequate generation for existing and new large loads.
frame_summary: FERC is arguing that existing wholesale tariffs are not adequate for large loads and must be rebuilt to connect them faster while protecting other customers from the costs of load that does not arrive.
verbatim_quote: Under the orders, each RTO/ISO, and its transmission owners have 60 days to either justify why their current tariffs remain just and reasonable without provisions tailored to large loads, or to file tariff changes that address the issues the Commission identified.
notes: Federal counterpart to the state-level moves; establishes that the commitment question is now a national tariff question.

title: First Statewide Moratorium on New Hyperscale Data Centers Launched by Governor Kathy Hochul
date_evidence:
July 14, 2026

Albany, NY

# First Statewide Moratorium on New Hyperscale Data Centers Launched by Governor Kathy Hochul
key_claim: New York paused discretionary state environmental permits for hyperscale data centres for up to a year and directed the Department of Public Service to consider a fund including an insurance pool that developers may have to contribute to as protection against speculative large loads.
frame_summary: New York is arguing that data-centre development has outrun any means of allocating its grid and ratepayer costs, so approvals should stop until commitment and cost-recovery standards exist.
verbatim_quote: The fund could support the procurement of new clean energy supply and establishment of an insurance pool to which developers may need to contribute to protect against speculative large loads that create uncertainty and increase costs.
notes: The pause covers discretionary DEC environmental permits, not every approval route; body prose reflects that limit.

title: Planners Have Tools to Manage Large Load Forecast Uncertainty. Are They Working?
date_evidence:
[Brief](https://rmi.org/resource-types/brief/) July 17, 2026

# Planners Have Tools to Manage Large Load Forecast Uncertainty. Are They Working?
key_claim: Where large-load tariffs imposed commitment tests, disclosed demand fell sharply: AEP Ohio's 30 GW of data-centre requests produced 5.6 GW of newly signed contracts, system-wide 2030 forecasts fell by roughly a third at AEP Ohio and about half at Indiana Michigan Power, over 80% of Georgia Power's 68 GW pipeline carries no binding commitment, and ERCOT counted only 37% of requested load in its 2030 adjusted forecast.
frame_summary: RMI is arguing that the gap between interconnection-queue volumes and real demand is measurable and already being closed by commitment screens, not an unknowable forecasting problem.
verbatim_quote: Prior to the tariff, data centers or developers had requested 30 GW of load — nearly three times AEP Ohio's typical peak demand of 10.5 GW. Under the tariff, only 5.6 GW of new data center contracts were signed, adding to the 12.2 GW already under contract, for a total of 17.8 GW of contracted data center projects expected to come online through 2035.
verbatim_list: For example, following the implementation of new tariffs for their large load customers, system-wide forecasted 2030 demand declined by roughly one-third in AEO Ohio and by about half in Indiana Michigan Power (Exhibit 3).

As of May 2026, the maximum potential 2032 demand from large loads in its pipeline exceeds 68 GW — roughly four times the utility's historic whole-system peak demand (Exhibit 2). Yet, more than 60 GW, over 80% of the pipeline, remains in early "technical review" stages, without binding contractual or financial commitments.
As a result, ERCOT's 2030 Adjusted Load Forecast included only 37% of the total requested load in its 2030 forecast (Exhibit 5), reflecting a more evidence-based projection.
notes: Spine source for the signal. The verbatim_list preserves RMI's own typo 'AEO Ohio' exactly as published.

title: Planning for Uncertain Data Center Demand
key_claim: Commissions can approve an initial tranche of resources tied to verified need and condition later tranches on signed service agreements, deposits, collateral postings and construction progress; distinguishing speculative inquiries from committed projects is the mechanism for reducing forecast error.
frame_summary: RMI is arguing that because large-load pipelines are systematically overstated, procurement should be staged against verified commitment milestones rather than sized to the queue.
verbatim_quote: Commissions can approve an initial tranche of resources tied to verified need, then condition later tranches on signed electric service agreements, deposits, collateral postings, interconnection milestones, construction progress, transmission availability, updated forecasts, or reserve margin needs.
notes: Published five days before the scan; supplies the adaptation pathway rather than the headline numbers.

title: Large Load Interconnection Requests Surge; ESIG Maps the Gaps
key_claim: Large-load interconnection processes are fragmented across regions and largely ungoverned nationally, with inadequate coordination between utilities and ISOs/RTOs producing duplicated effort and inconsistent visibility into cumulative system impacts.
frame_summary: ESIG is arguing that large-load interconnection sits where generator interconnection sat before FERC standardised it, and should move to cluster studies and a single federal procedure.
verbatim_quote: Interconnection requests have grown exponentially in number and magnitude, and the processes meant to manage them—the studies, the legal agreements, the procedural requirements—are fragmented across regions and largely ungoverned at the national level.
verbatim_list: Coordination between utilities and ISOs/RTOs, where necessary, is inadequate, creating duplicated effort and inconsistent visibility into cumulative system impacts.
notes: Explains why the same project can appear in several queues at once, which is the mechanical basis for duplication.

title: Exelon 'high probability' data center load falls 40%
key_claim: Exelon's high-probability data-centre load fell nearly 40% to about 11 GW in the second quarter from 18 GW at the end of last year as it entered transmission security agreements; about 4 GW of signed load has posted $1 billion in collateral, and the interconnection pipeline fell to about 25 GW from about 43 GW disclosed in May.
frame_summary: Utility Dive is reporting that a large regulated utility now treats a private contractual instrument, not a forecast, as the test of which data-centre demand is real.
verbatim_quote: The current high-probability projects — about 9 GW in ComEd’s territory in northern Illinois and 2 GW in Mid-Atlantic states — includeabout 4 GW of data center load with signed TSAs that have posted $1 billion in collateral, according to Jones.
verbatim_list: Exelon’s “high probability” data center load fell nearly 40%, to about 11 GW, in the second quarter from 18 GW at the end of last year, the Chicago-based utility company said Thursday.

Exelon’s data center interconnection pipeline — potential projects that utilities are studying or are about to study — fell to about 25 GW in the second quarter from about 43 GW disclosed during a May earnings conference call.
The TSAs include provisions designed to protect existing ratepayers from data center-related costs such as credit obligations, committed revenue contributions and shortfall payments.
notes: The 'includeabout' spacing error is in the published page and is preserved verbatim.

title: Data center approvals in Texas halted until audits completed, Gov. Greg Abbott says
key_claim: ERCOT is tracking more than 1,800 projects representing over 474 gigawatts, more than five times the grid's record peak demand, with approximately 90% of new power requests coming from data centres; projects failing the ordered audit should be denied connection.
frame_summary: The Texas Tribune is reporting that the state has made grid connection conditional on proving a project is real and self-supporting, rather than on queue position.
verbatim_quote: ERCOT is currently tracking more than 1,800 projects in the queue, representing over 474 gigawatts of electricity, or more than five times the grid’s record for peak demand, according to ERCOT. Approximately 90% of the new power requests are data centers, Abbott said.
notes: Carries the directive's headline numbers; used because the Governor's own PDF returned an empty body to the fetcher.
